closing.reason: What I tried: (1) Call sites. archive._object_stem is reached only through archive._object_key, whose only callers are the two encoders the diff changes. archive.to_s3/to_s3_parquet key by child oid, not bounds. pgpm_hypertable and pgpm_core/uninstall.sql derive no key from bounds. _refuse_empty_range parses the raw text in the same session _native_text does. (2) Tick, resume and upgrade paths. A tick hands canonical text, so it is unchanged. An id chunk recorded under a trailing-zero key (_100.0) is re-keyed _100 on the head, which cannot overwrite the recorded object, so there is no loss on upgrade. (3) Mutations. Each removes only its encoder's p_lo reading. The parquet mutant alone passes ACC-01 only because ACC-01 is NDJSON; test 54 part B covers parquet. Both mutations are sound. (4) The body's guarantee that 'from any DateStyle or TimeZone, the object key's stem is the stem of the instant the call's range read began at', and the new reference.md text that 'the range it reads, the recorded-chunk check and the key all take that one reading', BREAK on a date-column grid (V-01, run live in pgpm_prv-archive). The grid has partition_tz UTC with cells at 00:00Z. From an America/New_York session, archive_to_s3_ndjson('v1.d', null, '2024-01-02', '2024-01-03') reads the whole 2 January cell (2 rows), because the date column truncates the '2024-01-02 05:00:00+00' literal. The head keys that cell ..._2024010205000000, but the same call from UTC keys it ..._2024010200000000. So one chunk with the same rows gets two keys depending on the session zone, and the 05:00Z key starts no cell. That is #814's consequence (the key names an instant other than the chunk the object holds, and it varies by session). The recorded-chunk check looks up the session-shaped key, so it never meets a ledger row at the cell's real key. The base keyed both calls 2024010200000000: V-01 passes on the base and fails 3 defect checks on the head, with every LIVENESS holding. It is a regression in the code the PR covers, Tier 3 (a documented contract not kept, no overwrite: no cell starts at the stray key). _encode_upload_parquet takes the same path. Naive-timestamp and timestamptz grids keep the guarantee; only the date column's truncation splits the read from the key.
